Hi Sally —

Really appreciate the quick follow-up and glad the demo landed well. Short answers up front: 

- We can provisionally hold a price for a short window (typically 14 days) while legal reviews, but the committed per-token rate at mid-tier (500M tokens/mo) requires an executed DPA and acceptable SOC2 evidence to be in place for billing/credits to be honored.

- Acceptable evidence: SOC2 Type II report (preferred) OR a signed attestation from your security team that maps to the controls we require. AICPA bridge letters are acceptable in some cases — we can review. For most customers SOC2 Type II + DPA execution is the cleanest path.

- Typical internal acceptance timeline at Redwood: 3–5 business days after we receive the report + completed attestation checklist. If legal redlines the DPA that can add time; we try to parallelize review so evidence receipt and DPA countersign are often concurrent.

I’ve attached our standard pricing matrix and a draft DPA (docx redline-friendly). If you’re open, I’ll loop in our pricing lead (Marissa) and security/compliance (Stephanie) to make the acceptance path explicit and see if we can shorten the acceptance window for you.

Proposed next steps: 
- You share the SOC2 report or attestation link + any procurement timelines.
- We provide a conditional pricing confirmation email (holds price for 14 days) and start parallel review of your legal redlines.
- If all good within the 14-day hold, we execute and apply credits retro back to the commit start date as discussed.

Attachments: pricing-matrix-q3-2026.xlsx (pricing matrix), Redwood-DPA-v1.docx (draft)

Best,
